key_insight: AI models identified signals of vision-threatening diabetic retinopathy and advanced AMD in external eye photographs, while fairness training partially reduced demographic performance disparities.
clinical_relevance: External eye photography may offer a research pathway for assessing posterior eye disease, but these models are not yet suitable for clinical deployment.
method: Compared convolutional networks, a vision transformer, and a fine-tuned LLaVA vision-language model.
Evaluated disease classification using AUC and demographic fairness using equity-scaled AUC.
Applied five fairness-training strategies to the best-performing models.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used 40,687 photographs from 9,878 patients at one institution; baseline AUCs reached 85.4% for vision-threatening diabetic retinopathy and 86.3% for advanced AMD, versus 67–74% for glaucoma.
watch_item: Single-institution, proof-of-concept findings require external validation, and fairness training did not eliminate demographic disparities.
paper_title: Applications of Fairness Training in Artificial Intelligence to Ophthalmic Disease Diagnosis using External Eye Photographs
